body:
Myk's call (2026-08-22, workshopping the v3 arc): containers and federation are crucial and
they stretch the beginner tutorial past a comfortable shape — "maybe we should have a beginners
tutorial and an advanced tutorial?" Settled direction: yes, two arcs. "A Store of Your Own"
(tutorial v3, spec 48) stays complete in one tab and one pair of hands; the advanced journey is
its own designed sequel, not a stretched epilogue.

The sequel's likely engine, to be designed properly at P1: "your store meets Rae's store" — two
peers side by side, which the in-tab single-store format cannot stage honestly. Candidate
material: containers as the capability boundary, opening a federation channel (names are the
receiver's), blessing and cursing a peer's law, dropping a channel with the two-sided proof,
and what erasure means across two stores (the §11 boundary stated honestly). The beginner arc's
last screen trails it: "Rae's getting a store of their own. That's the next journey."

Format question for P1: two browser peers in one page, or a tab peer plus a served store? The
two-laptop demo script (the vision doc) and the village are prior art. The T143 rule binds:
every lesson earns a story rail that drives the real surface.

Acceptance criteria (design phase):
(a) A working spec at .adlc/specs/NN-advanced-tutorial.md opening with user stories, criteria
    naming their rails, following spec 48's conventions (observe predicates, plain language,
    the glossary contract continuing from the beginner glossary). Verify: `adlc spec-lint` on
    the working spec.
(b) The format decision (two in-page peers vs tab+served) is made with a reasoned
    recommendation and Myk's word. Verify: the spec PR review.

Merge tier: DESIGN-STAGE — Myk's merge, after the beginner tutorial (T211/T106) ships.
title: The advanced tutorial — two stores, containers, federation: a designed sequel (DESIGN-STAGE)
